title: Implement pkg/testutils -- DiffTest struct and RunDiffTests (prd001 R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component section and design decision 2)
  - go.mod (module name for import paths)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: "DiffTest struct, Normalize type, FileExpectation struct, RunDiffTests function, TimestampNormalizer"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement the DiffTest struct per prd001 R1.1-R1.4 with fields: Args []string, Stdin []byte (nil means EOF immediately), Env []string (nil means inherit the test process environment), ExitCode int, Normalize []Normalize, and FileExpectations []FileExpectation."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) per prd001 R2.1-R2.5. Run each DiffTest as a named subtest (t.Run). Execute both binaries with identical Args, Stdin, Env, and a per-test working directory created by t.TempDir(). Capture stdout, stderr, and exit code from each binary independently. Enforce a 10-second default timeout per binary invocation via context.WithTimeout."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement comparison and divergence reporting per prd001 R3.1-R3.6. Apply each Normalize function in the slice to both binaries stdout and stderr in order, then compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte, normalized stderr byte-for-byte, and exit codes exactly. On any divergence call t.Errorf with: Args, Stdin truncated to 256 bytes, reference stdout, Go stdout, reference stderr, Go stderr, both exit codes."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement the Normalize function type (func([]byte) []byte) per prd001 R4.1 and R4.3. The Normalize field on DiffTest is a slice. When the slice is nil or empty, no transformation is applied. RunDiffTests applies each function in the slice in sequence, passing the output of one as input to the next."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement TimestampNormalizer per prd001 R4.2. It must replace strftime-format timestamp patterns matching the ts default format (e.g., 'Feb 19 12:34:56') with the fixed placeholder string 'TIMESTAMP'. Use a compiled regexp that covers month abbreviations, day, and HH:MM:SS."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement file-state comparison per prd001 R5.1-R5.2. Add FileExpectation struct with fields Path string (relative to working directory) and Content []byte. After both binaries exit, for each FileExpectation in the test case, read the actual file from the Go binary's working directory and compare its content byte-for-byte against Content. Report divergence with expected and actual file bytes in the same style as stdout divergence."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Primary source file is pkg/testutils/difftest.go, not testutils.go. The primary exported type is DiffTest so the file is named difftest.go per the project file naming convention (testutils/testutils.go is explicitly forbidden by the project constitution)."
  - id: D2
    text: "The Normalize field on DiffTest is []Normalize (a slice), not a single function, per prd001 R4.3. RunDiffTests composes the slice by applying each function in sequence to both binaries stdout and stderr independently."
  - id: D3
    text: "Timeout is enforced per prd001 R2.3 via context.WithTimeout with a fixed 10-second default. Each binary runs in its own goroutine; if exec.CommandContext is cancelled by the deadline, the test fails with a message naming the binary and the test case. Do not make the timeout configurable -- the PRD fixes it at 10 seconds."
  - id: D4
    text: "FileExpectation.Path is relative to the working directory of the binary invocation (t.TempDir() per test). RunDiffTests reads the file from the Go binary working directory for comparison. Reference binary working directory is separate; its file output is not checked against FileExpectation."
  - id: D5
    text: "Do not emit any output to the test process stdout or stderr during a passing run per prd001 R2.4. All reporting goes through t.Errorf or t.Fatalf so that go test output is clean on success."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "DiffTest struct has all required fields (Args []string, Stdin []byte, Env []string, ExitCode int, Normalize []Normalize, FileExpectations []FileExpectation) and compiles without error."
  - id: AC2
    text: "RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests) executes both binaries with identical Args, Stdin, and Env and captures stdout, stderr, and exit code from each independently."
  - id: AC3
    text: "On stdout divergence, the failure message includes the DiffTest Args, the first 256 bytes of Stdin, the reference binary stdout, the Go binary stdout, both stderrs, and both exit codes."
  - id: AC4
    text: "TimestampNormalizer('Feb 19 12:34:56 hello') returns a string where the timestamp prefix is replaced with 'TIMESTAMP', producing output that contains 'TIMESTAMP hello'."
  - id: AC5
    text: "A binary invocation that exceeds 10 seconds causes the subtest to fail with a clear timeout message and does not block the test run indefinitely."
  - id: AC6
    text: "A DiffTest with a FileExpectation whose Content differs from the file the Go binary writes causes RunDiffTests to call t.Errorf with both the expected and actual file contents."
  - id: AC7
    text: "go build ./pkg/testutils/... succeeds with no errors on both darwin/arm64 and linux/amd64."

title: Implement cmd/ts: timestamp stdin lines (prd004-ts R1-R8)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml (full PRD, all requirements)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (cmd/ component description, technology choices)
  - docs/specs/sources.yaml (ts Perl source reference for flag behavior)

files:
  - path: cmd/ts/main.go
    action: create
    note: "Complete ts implementation: flag parsing, strftime formatting, all flag modes (-i, -s, -m, -r), stdin loop"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default mode (prd004-ts R1): read stdin line by line with bufio.Scanner; prepend timestamp using default format '%b %d %H:%M:%S' evaluated at the time each line is received; write '<timestamp> <line>' to stdout and flush after each line; preserve original newline; pass through partial last line (no trailing newline) with timestamp prefix; exit 0 on clean EOF; do not exit non-zero on SIGPIPE."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement custom format string (prd004-ts R2): accept optional positional argument as a strftime format string; implement strftime by mapping standard specifiers to Go time.Format equivalents; implement ts-specific subsecond extensions %.S (seconds.microseconds, e.g. '32.001234'), %.s (Unix epoch.microseconds), %.T (HH:MM:SS.microseconds) by detecting them before format conversion and sampling time.Now() once per line for both second and microsecond components (prd004-ts R2.4)."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement incremental mode -i (prd004-ts R3): timestamp shows elapsed time since previous line (first line shows elapsed since startup); use default format '%H:%M:%S' in -i mode; apply TZ=GMT for elapsed display by converting elapsed seconds to time.Unix(elapsedSeconds, 0).UTC() before formatting; -i and -s are mutually exclusive -- print usage to stderr and exit non-zero when both are given."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement elapsed-since-start mode -s (prd004-ts R4): timestamp shows time elapsed since ts started, monotonically increasing across all lines; use default format '%H:%M:%S' with TZ=GMT (same approach as -i); a custom format argument overrides the default."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement monotonic clock mode -m (prd004-ts R5): use time.Now() for all timestamp sampling -- Go's time.Now() automatically carries a monotonic reading, so -m requires no additional mechanism beyond documenting this invariant; compatible with all format modes (-i, -s, default) and custom formats including subsecond extensions."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement relative-time conversion mode -r (prd004-ts R6): scan each input line for the four timestamp patterns from prd004-ts R6.2 (syslog 'Jan  5 14:30:00', ISO-8601 '2024-01-05T14:30:00.000Z', RFC 2822 '16 Jun 94 07:29:35 GMT', lastlog 'Mon Jan  5 14:30'); replace matched timestamp with a human-readable relative age string (e.g. '15m5s ago'); when -r and a format string are both given, replace matched timestamp with the strftime-formatted time instead of a relative string; pass through lines with no recognized timestamp unchanged; -r is mutually exclusive with -i and -s."
  - id: R7
    text: "Implement exit codes and error handling (prd004-ts R7): exit 0 on clean stdin EOF; print usage message to stderr and exit non-zero on unrecognized flag; install a SIGPIPE handler so the process exits 0 rather than producing a write error when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer."
  - id: R8
    text: "Implement environment handling (prd004-ts R8): respect TZ environment variable for wall-clock timestamp formatting in default mode and custom format mode (non -i/-s); override with UTC internally for -i and -s elapsed formatting regardless of user TZ setting."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Implement strftime() as a Go function that replaces format specifiers with Go time.Format layout strings. Handle subsecond extensions %.S, %.s, %.T by scanning the format string before conversion, extracting microseconds from the sampled time.Now() value, and substituting them as formatted decimal strings. Sample time.Now() exactly once per line and use that single value for both the second and microsecond components (prd004-ts R2.4)."
  - id: D2
    text: "For -i and -s elapsed display, convert the elapsed duration to a time.Time by calling time.Unix(int64(elapsed.Seconds()), 0).UTC(). This makes time.Format('%H:%M:%S') produce the correct elapsed string (e.g. '00:00:05' for 5 seconds) without locale or timezone interference, matching Perl's TZ=GMT behavior (prd004-ts R3.2, R4.2)."
  - id: D3
    text: "Use the standard flag package for -i, -s, -m, -r flag parsing. The optional positional format string is taken from flag.Args()[0] after flag.Parse(). Set flag.Usage to print a usage string to stderr. An unrecognized flag causes flag.Parse() to call flag.Usage() and os.Exit(2), which satisfies prd004-ts R7.2."
  - id: D4
    text: "For -r mode, precompile the four timestamp patterns from prd004-ts R6.2 using regexp.MustCompile at package init. To compute a relative age string, parse the matched timestamp into a time.Time, compute time.Since(parsed), and format the duration using a human-readable formatter (e.g. '15m5s ago'). When both -r and a format string are given, use strftime(format, parsed) instead of the relative age string (prd004-ts R6.3)."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "'go build ./cmd/ts/' succeeds and produces a binary with no compilation errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "echo 'hello world' | ./ts produces one line matching the pattern '<Month> <DD> <HH:MM:SS> hello world' using the default format."
  - id: AC3
    text: "printf 'a\\nb\\nc\\n' | ./ts -s produces three lines with non-decreasing elapsed timestamps in HH:MM:SS format."
  - id: AC4
    text: "./ts -i -s prints a usage message to stderr and exits with a non-zero exit code."
  - id: AC5
    text: "./ts --invalid prints a usage message to stderr and exits with a non-zero exit code."
  - id: AC6
    text: "printf '' | ./ts exits 0 and writes nothing to stdout."
  - id: AC7
    text: "printf 'partial' | ./ts (stdin with no trailing newline) produces exactly one line prefixed with a timestamp and no extra newline appended."
  - id: AC8
    text: "'go vet ./cmd/ts/' reports no issues and golangci-lint run ./cmd/ts/ reports no warnings."

title: Implement cmd/ts differential tests (prd004-ts R9)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml (R9 differential testing requirements)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.0.yaml (all 13 test cases with inputs and expected outputs)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (DiffTest struct contract R1, RunDiffTests R2-R3, TimestampNormalizer R4)
  - cmd/ts/main.go (binary entry point being tested -- must exist before this task runs)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (RunDiffTests and TimestampNormalizer API -- must exist before this task runs)

files:
  - path: cmd/ts/ts_test.go
    action: create
    note: differential tests for cmd/ts against the reference ts binary using pkg/testutils.RunDiffTests

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement TestMain in cmd/ts/ts_test.go that builds the cmd/ts binary into a temp directory via exec.Command(\"go\", \"build\", \"-o\", goBinaryPath, \".\") before any test runs. Store the resulting binary path in a package-level variable. Locate the reference binary ts using exec.LookPath(\"ts\"); call m.Run() and skip all tests with t.Skip if ts is not found."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement TestTs(t *testing.T) that defines a []testutils.DiffTest slice covering all 13 test cases from test-rel01.0 and calls testutils.RunDiffTests(t, goBinaryPath, refBinaryPath, tests). Each DiffTest entry must have a Name field matching the test-rel01.0 test case name exactly: default_format_three_lines, default_format_empty_stdin, default_format_partial_last_line, custom_strftime_format, subsecond_format_dotS, elapsed_since_start_mode, incremental_mode, incremental_and_elapsed_mutually_exclusive, monotonic_clock_mode, relative_mode_syslog_timestamp, relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough, invalid_flag, tz_environment_respected (prd004-ts R9.2)."
  - id: R3
    text: "Apply pkg/testutils.TimestampNormalizer (a slice of Normalize functions per prd001-testutils R4.3) to all DiffTest cases whose stdout contains wall-clock timestamps: default_format_three_lines, default_format_partial_last_line, custom_strftime_format, subsecond_format_dotS, elapsed_since_start_mode, incremental_mode, monotonic_clock_mode, relative_mode_syslog_timestamp, and tz_environment_respected. Set Normalize to nil for default_format_empty_stdin, relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough, incremental_and_elapsed_mutually_exclusive, and invalid_flag (prd004-ts R9.1)."
  - id: R4
    text: "Set the Env field on each DiffTest to include LC_ALL=C. For tz_environment_respected, also include TZ=UTC. For elapsed_since_start_mode and incremental_mode, also include TZ=GMT to match the Perl reference behavior (prd004-ts R3.2, R4.2, R8.1)."
  - id: R5
    text: "For incremental_and_elapsed_mutually_exclusive and invalid_flag, set ExpectedExitCode to a non-zero value. These cases must verify that the process exits non-zero; do not apply normalization. For all other cases, set ExpectedExitCode to 0 (prd004-ts R3.4, R7.2)."
  - id: R6
    text: "Set Stdin to the correct []byte for each test case as specified in test-rel01.0. For default_format_empty_stdin, set Stdin to []byte{} (empty but non-nil, per prd001-testutils R1.2). For test cases with no stdin (nil in test-rel01.0), set Stdin to nil."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "TimestampNormalizer from pkg/testutils replaces strftime-formatted timestamp prefixes with a fixed placeholder. Pass it as a slice ([]testutils.Normalize{testutils.TimestampNormalizer}) in the Normalize field of each DiffTest that requires normalization, per prd001-testutils R4.3."
  - id: D2
    text: "Build the binary in TestMain using os.MkdirTemp for a throwaway directory and defer os.RemoveAll to clean up after all tests complete. Set the package-level variable before calling m.Run()."
  - id: D3
    text: "The Args field in each DiffTest must contain only the flags and positional arguments passed to the binary -- do not include the binary name itself. The binary paths are passed separately to RunDiffTests per prd001-testutils R2.1."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "go test ./cmd/ts/... passes with no failures when both the Go ts binary builds successfully and the reference ts binary (from moreutils) is on PATH."
  - id: AC2
    text: "All 13 test cases from test-rel01.0 are present as named DiffTest entries. The Name field of each entry matches the test_case name from test-rel01.0 exactly."
  - id: AC3
    text: "When the reference ts binary is not found on PATH, all tests are skipped via t.Skip with a message indicating ts is not installed, rather than failing."
  - id: AC4
    text: "TimestampNormalizer is applied to every test case that produces wall-clock timestamp output. Test cases with deterministic or error output have nil normalization."
  - id: AC5
    text: "cmd/ts/ts_test.go compiles with no warnings under golangci-lint."
